metadata.title: Prohibition on Wholesaling Under Section 503B of the Federal Food, Drug, and Cosmetic Act
metadata.topic: Draft guideline · FDA human drugs and biologics
metadata.legal_basis: FDA Guidance Document (21 CFR 10.115). Guidance states FDA's current thinking and is not binding unless a statute or regulation requires it; the official text governs.

candidates.statement: In general, FDA’s guidance documents do not establish legally enforceable responsibilities. 27 Instead, guidances describe the Agency’s current thinking on a topic and should be viewed only 28 as recommendations, unless specific regulatory or statutory requirements are cited. The use of 29 the word should in Agency guidances means that something is suggested or recommended, but 30 not required. 31
candidates.context: Under section 503B of the Federal Food, Drug, and Cosmetic Act (FD&C Act) (21 U.S.C. 17 353b), a drug compounded by an outsourcing facility 2 qualifies for exemptions from certain 18 statutory requirements if, among other conditions, the drug “will not be sold or transferred by an 19 entity other than the outsourcing facility that compounded such drug.” 3 However, this provision 20 “does not prohibit administration of a drug in a health care setting or dispensing a drug pursuant 21 to a prescription executed in accordance with section 503(b)(1).” 4 This guidance describes 22 FDA’s interpretation of, and policies concerning, the prohibition on wholesaling in section 503B 23 of the FD&C Act. candidates.statement: Similarly, the prohibition on wholesaling helps to preserve the integrity of the drug approval 82 process. Approval of a new drug means that FDA has determined that it is safe and effective and 83 that it was manufactured by a facility with appropriate methods used in, and facilities and 84 controls used for, preserving the drug’s identity, strength, quality, and purity to produce a high- 85 quality product. 13 Approval of new, innovative treatments can save lives, and approval of 86 generic drug products can increase access to critical therapies. If an outsourcing facility could 87 manufacture drug products for further sale or transfer by, for example, wholesale distributors, the 88 outsourcing facility would more closely resemble a conventional manufacturer whose drug 89 products are subject to new drug approval requirements. Section 503B of the FD&C Act 90 therefore imposes conditions which reduce the risk that conventional manufacturers would forgo 91 seeking FDA approval of their drug products to instead market unapproved, compounded drugs 92 as an outsourcing facility. Because the typical supply chain for approved drug products involves 93 wholesaling, consisting of multiple transfers between the manufacture of the drug and ultimately 94 dispensing or administering it to a patient, section 503B’s prohibition on wholesaling helps 95 reduce the incentive to compound drugs as an outsourcing facility rather than seek premarket 96 approval. 97

candidates.statement: Finally, because drugs compounded by outsourcing facilities in accordance with the conditions 99 of section 503B of the FD&C Act are exempt from drug supply chain security requirements in 100 section 582 of the FD&C Act, the prohibition on wholesaling is an important control to protect 101 the drug supply chain. Conditioning the exemption from section 582 on limitations on the sale 102 or transfer of a compounded drug reduces supply chain concerns such as diversion. The short 103 supply chain required under section 503B also makes it easier to associate the compounded drug 104 with the relevant outsourcing facility in the case of an adverse event or product quality issue. 105 We further note that outsourcing facilities are required to report adverse events to FDA. 14

candidates.statement: Drugs compounded by outsourcing facilities must meet the conditions in section 503B of the 202 FD&C Act, including the prohibition on wholesaling under section 503B(a)(8), to be eligible for 203 the statutory exemptions available under that section. This guidance provides FDA’s policies 204 concerning the prohibition on wholesaling, as explained in section III.A. In general, as described 205 in section III.A.1 and 2, the wholesaling provision applies to the sale or transfer of a 206 compounded drug by an entity other than the outsourcing facility that compounded the drug. As 207 described in section III.A.3, the prohibition on wholesaling does not apply to the administration 208 of a compounded drug in a health care setting or dispensing a compounded drug pursuant to a 209 prescription in accordance with section 503(b)(1) of the FD&C Act. None of the scenarios in 210 section III.B.1 involve, among other things, administration of a drug in a health care setting or 211 dispensing pursuant to a prescription in accordance with section 503(b)(1), so the exception to 212 the prohibition on wholesaling would not apply to any of them. 213

candidates.statement: Pursuant to section 704(a) of the FD&C Act, during inspections of outsourcing facilities, FDA 373 reviews records, such as contractual agreements, distribution data, shipment data, and customer 374 lists to evaluate compliance with section 503B(a)(8) of the FD&C Act. 27 If the Agency identifies 375 agreements or procedures concerning a third party’s sale or transfer of the outsourcing facility’s 376 compounded drugs that are not limited to administration in a health care setting or dispensing 377 pursuant to a prescription in accordance with section 503(b)(1), FDA may consider pursuing 378 regulatory or enforcement action against the outsourcing facility because drugs that are not 379 compounded in accordance with the conditions of section 503B of the FD&C Act are subject to 380 the requirements of sections 505, 502(f)(1), and 582 of the FD&C Act. The third party that sold 381 or transferred the outsourcing facility’s drugs may also be subject to regulatory or enforcement 382 action for distributing or causing the distribution of drugs in violation of section 301 of the 383 FD&C Act. 384
